pre_stated_reading: Synthetic and small: report as an external-author check only, never as real-world accuracy.
Scam recall (n=16) is counts only (n < 30); legitimate rates (n=22) are counts only (n < 30).
B4-engine runs in rule-only mode, so it cannot return NO_STRONG_SIGNALS; its legitimate items can only be LIKELY_SCAM (false alarm) or UNCLEAR.
A B4-engine recall clearly below its own-author synthetic recall (9/12) would indicate the rules are fitted to their author's phrasing; 'clearly' means the two Wilson intervals do not overlap.
No rule, threshold, prompt or code is changed in response to the result; findings feed the next rule-pack version, which needs a different evaluation set.
Primary comparison (protocol §6): B4-engine+llm vs B3-llm on dangerous misses and false alarms, paired campaign bootstrap at 97.5%; a difference is claimed only if its interval excludes 0.
The model is a small local model chosen for privacy and hardware, not for accuracy; B3's result describes this model and prompt only, not LLMs in general.
